Rollback

You might say

When a new version sends login error rate sharply up, roll back to the last known-good version; then confirm both running version and metrics recover.

Rollback restores a system or configuration to a previous known-good state to stop current impact.·If v2 causes abnormal login errors, switch the running image or configuration back to v1 and check the live version, login result, and error rate recover. It aims to reduce impact first. Fixing the issue and shipping a new version later is a forward fix, not rollback.

↳Rollback switches immediately to an existing older artifact; it does not wait for a forward fix.

Rollback success needs two kinds of evidence

Restore a known-good state to reduce impact: When a new version materially affects people, returning to a verified version or configuration can stop spread quickly. State the target clearly rather than saying only “restore it.”

A completed switch is not recovered health: First confirm the target version is actually running, then inspect login success, error rate, or key action recovery. If metrics do not recover, the problem may extend beyond this version.

What it is not

Rollback is not fixing code and shipping another version; that is a forward fix. It also differs from disabling a feature flag: a flag stops one new path, while rollback restores a whole version or configuration to a prior state.
